settings.name_in_paper: Quantum Best Arm Identification (quantum agent and quantum environment)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Quantum oracle access: the agent queries the environment via unitary oracles O_e and O_f in superposition.
unmapped: environment accessed through quantum unitary oracles (superposition queries over actions and environment states)
settings.definition_quote: we define a composite Hilbert space $\Hi = \Hi_X\otimes\Hi_Y$ ... prepare the state of the environment in a superposition $\ket{\psi_x} = \sum_{y \in Y} \sqrt{\nu_x(y)} \ket{y}$ ... we build the oracle $O_f$ on the composite Hilbert space of the agent and the environment

symbols.A_star: |<x*|A|0>|^2, initial amplitude-squared of the optimal action
symbols.p_q: p = sin(theta)^2, probability of a good (reward-1) outcome in the initial state
symbols.P_n: probability QBAI recommends the optimal action after n oracle rounds

source.label: th:main_theorem
source.quote: The probability $P_{n}(\tilde x)$ that QBAI will recommend the optimal action $\tilde x$ is maximized when $n \approx \frac{\pi}{4}\sqrt{1/p} - \frac{1}{2}$. It follows that {$P_{n}(\tilde x ) = \abs{\bra{\tilde x }A\ket{0}}^2\frac{a^*}{p}$}.

results.notes: Statement is an exact value of the success probability (recommendation probability of the optimal arm), not an error bound; quantity 'other', probability field set to 'expectation' only because the schema forces a value. With uniform A, success probability a*/(N E_X[a_x]) after about (pi/4)/sqrt(E_X[a_x]) rounds. Out of scope (quantum oracle).
